about: Reviewed differences between the recorded Go API responses (parity/blackbox/api-recorded.jsonl) and the Rust engine, for crates/maverick-api/tests/replay.rs (bead 5.15). Every rule and entry names its DIVERGENCES row. A rule turns an approved difference into an exact comparison: strip removes Rust-only members from our body, recorded_replace rewrites the recorded body where a row changes a value, mask rewrites both where a row leaves text to a library. An entry exempts named parts of one recorded exchange. Anything not covered here must match byte for byte after the README section 5 masking.

rules.reason: Recommend entries gain low_availability (D8), retention_mode (D9), settings (D14), execution_alias_retention (D15), and param_constraints (D29); the response gains zero_retention (D9) and telemetry (D39). Additive: the Go members are unchanged.
Catalog entries gain the retention fields (D1), execution_alias_retention (D15), and param_constraints (D29) after Go's eleven keys. Additive.
An MCP recommend_model result carries the POST /v1/recommend body (text and structuredContent), so it gains the same additive members.
An MCP list_models result carries the GET /v1/models body, so its entries gain the same additive members.

A tool-argument validation error keeps the isError shape and the 'validating "arguments": ' prefix; the validator's own text after it comes from the jsonschema crate. crates/maverick-api/tests/mcp.rs checks that it names the offending property.
The tenant's constraints gain telemetry_opt_out (D39) and affinity_cost_aware (D44), both default false, as their last members. Additive.
A 2xx item with no check_pass derives completed_unchecked, not success. Items with check_pass keep Go's outcome.
The outcome filter accepts completed_unchecked (the D16 outcome of an unchecked 2xx), so its 422 message lists it among the outcomes.
The engine-authored prefix 'malformed request body: ' is kept (D25, a case of the general D36 rule); the decoder's own text after it is Rust's (serde_json), not Go's encoding/json.

The job-queue component is job_queue (graphile_worker), not river_queues; with no worker registered it reads no_workers with graphile_worker wording. Component keys stay sorted. D49 adds role=origin to the hosted response.
recorded_replace: "provider_client_config":(\{[^{}]*\}),"river_queues":\{"status":"no_workers","detail":"no River worker has registered a queue"\}

rules.reason: A recommend request without mode ranks in quality mode (D47), so the response's mode is quality where Go said balanced, and the MCP recommend_model schema says default quality. The request decides it, so the rule skips any recorded request that names a mode.

MCP recommend_model takes the optional affinity object of POST /v1/recommend (D44), so its tools/list input schema gains an affinity property after constraints. The other tools and schema members are unchanged.
